components: rounded looped head above the main line
strokeOrder: loop clockwise around the rounded head above the main line
continue down and left through the deep bowl without lifting
after one lift, place the upper-right dot
after another lift, place the upper-left dot

strokeOrderSource.citation: Zer o Zabar, Fe, qāf, ṭe, ḍāl, and ṛe, independent ق calligraphic and handwriting animations and Qāf instructions (Northwestern University Libraries Open Textbook, 2026)
strokeOrderSource.variation: The independent-form animations draw the rounded looped head and deep leftward bowl in one uninterrupted body stroke, then place the upper-right dot and the upper-left dot as separate runs: three strokes separated by two pen lifts. The adjacent prose identifies qāf as fe with a second dot and says its independent and final bowl is much deeper than fe's. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the body-first, right-to-left dot order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback. The provenance remains Urdu-specific rather than borrowing the separate Persian or Arabic ق sources.

notes: Qāf sounds q and has a much deeper independent and final bowl than fe ف.
